content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs against the disclosure and the single USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of all 22 claims (independent claims 1, 13, 18 and dependents 2-12, 14-17, 19-22), every entry in the numeral ledger (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94), every structural, material, positional, and operational statement in the Summary and Detailed Description, the Abstract, and every sentence of the FIG. 1-7 briefs was matched against exact affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is truncated mid-sentence at "The difference between" but is fully subsumed by the disclosure). Confirmed traced: rail/upper face/lower face/longitudinal slot/printed distance marks; fixed fence at the first end, perpendicular to the rail, downwardly projecting portion bearing on the edge, reversibility by two screws in two corresponding holes moving that portion from one longitudinal side to the opposite side with the same marked face in use; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate carriages with lower keys in the slot preventing rotation while permitting sliding; one cylindrical drill bushing per carriage with a vertical bore through the carriage registering with the slot; both bore axes parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob above the rail with a shank through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, tightening clamping the rail between carriage and shoe; per-carriage pointers aligned with their bore axes and read against the same marks, their difference being center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index and sighted on a pencil centerline; the full method sequence; hardened-metal replaceable bushings and rigid-polymer-or-metal remaining parts; and the no-motor/battery/sensor/network limitation. Internal consistency checks passed: section line 3-3 carries the same repeated designation in the FIG. 2 brief, the FIG. 3 brief, the Brief Description, and the Detailed Description (through the second guide carriage 70), and line 5-5 likewise (through the first guide carriage 50), with both endpoints inside the drawing area and paired arrows; every numeral has one meaning and appears in at least one figure brief and in the Detailed Description with matching parenthetical figure citations; every figure FIG. 1-7 is referenced in the description; the title, "Not applicable" cross-reference, and "Not applicable" government-support statement match input/brief.md (no priority claim, no federally sponsored research); the preserved terminology list is used throughout; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative, or "by way of example"/"any closed outline" shape-justifying text remains; the abstract is a single paragraph of about 148 words. Two findings are reported: one critical source-fidelity defect in the FIG. 1 brief, which verbalizes a rail-to-workpiece-edge angular relationship ("running lengthwise parallel to that edge") that no inventor passage states and that sits in tension with the source's own and the claims' "the rail extends inward across the front face"; and one minor claim formality (claim 10 re-introducing "a body" of each carriage already recited in parent claim 9). Prior-art characterizations in the Background were not traced to inventor sources, as instructed, and no rendered images were inspected.

findings.title: FIG. 1 brief asserts that the rail runs parallel to the workpiece edge, an angular relationship the inventor never states
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, first paragraph describing the rail ("A long straight rail 10 rests on the front face of the workpiece 90, spaced inward from the workpiece edge 92 and running lengthwise parallel to that edge...")
findings.detail: The orientation of the rail relative to the reference edge is substantive technical matter: it determines whether sliding a carriage along the slot changes the setback of a hole, and it is the geometry on which the fence-versus-pointer division of function depends. No affirmative USER passage states that the rail is parallel to the workpiece edge. The only source statement about rail-to-edge orientation is the opposite-leaning "the rail extends inward across the workpiece when the fence bears against the edge," which the draft itself carries into claim 13 ("so that the rail extends inward across the front face") and claim 18 (same wording) and into the Detailed Description ("the rail 10 extends inward across the front face of the workpiece 90"). The source is genuinely unresolved on this point: the reversibility passage places the projecting portion on a longitudinal side of the rail, while the center-index-plus-sight-notch passage requires a single centerline to pass through two points spaced apart along the rail. The figure brief resolves that ambiguity by verbalizing a specific angular relationship, which is an invention assertion rather than a depiction convention, and it is not confined to a shape-neutral outline. This is not curable by adding an example or optional-embodiment statement to the application text. Note for the fix's coherence: the two following sentences of the same brief (the fence "crosses the rail 10 transverse to its length, reaching from the rail 10 toward the workpiece edge 92" and portion 32 "stands on the longitudinal side of the rail 10 that faces the workpiece edge 92... and contacts the workpiece edge 92") are each independently traceable to the disclosure ("The fence is perpendicular to the rail"; "moves the downwardly projecting part of the fence from one longitudinal side of the rail to the opposite longitudinal side"; "bears against one straight edge of the workpiece") and should be left intact, so the view remains fully specified without the untraced parallelism statement. The FIG. 4 brief does not verbalize any angular relationship and needs no change.
findings.evidence: Candidate wording (figures/FIG-1.md): "A long straight rail 10 rests on the front face of the workpiece 90, spaced inward from the workpiece edge 92 and running lengthwise parallel to that edge, well inside the drawing area." Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md), which shows the gap rather than supporting it: "The fence is perpendicular to the rail, so the rail extends inward across the workpiece when the fence bears against the edge." No passage in input/disclosure.md or the USER passage of input/conversation.md states that the rail is parallel to, or at any stated angle to, the workpiece edge.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, delete the untraced angular clause so the sentence reads: "A long straight rail 10 rests on the front face of the workpiece 90, spaced inward from the workpiece edge 92, well inside the drawing area." Make no addition to draft/07-drawings.md or draft/08-detailed-description.md.

findings.title: Claim 10 re-introduces "a body" of each guide carriage already recited in parent claim 9
findings.detail: Claim 9 already recites that the drill bushing of each of the first and second guide carriages "is received in a body of that guide carriage as a separate piece." Claim 10, which depends from claim 9, then recites "a body of the first guide carriage, a body of the second guide carriage" with the indefinite article, which reads as introducing second, different bodies and creates an antecedent-basis/double-inclusion ambiguity about which body is made of rigid polymer or metal. The underlying material limitation is fully supported by the disclosure ("The rail, fence, carriage bodies, shoes, spacer plate, pointers, and knobs may be made from rigid polymer or metal"), so only the article needs correcting. Claim 17 correctly uses "a body of that guide carriage" because it depends from claim 13, which does not recite a carriage body.
findings.evidence: Claim 9: "...is received in a body of that guide carriage as a separate piece that is withdrawable from that guide carriage..." Claim 10: "wherein the rail, the fence, a body of the first guide carriage, a body of the second guide carriage, the clamping shoe of each guide carriage, the first pointer, the second pointer, and the clamp knob of each guide carriage are of rigid polymer or metal."
findings.fix: In claim 10, replace "a body of the first guide carriage, a body of the second guide carriage" with "the body of the first guide carriage, the body of the second guide carriage".
